analyst_view.overall: Le Havre are 18th with 2 points and no league win, and interim coach Jair Karam takes charge after Didier Digard was removed; he has called for a 'union sacree' and wants to restore defensive stability. Lorient (11th, 12 pts) under Alexandre Dujeux have the league's best defence (8 conceded, five clean sheets) but its worst attack (7 scored), and lost 2-0 at Brest on Monday. Le Havre are without the suspended Ayumu Seko and Rassoul Ndiaye is a doubt with a thigh problem; Lorient are missing their top assister Panos Katseris, with Ibrahima Balde doubtful.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Lorient have scored only 7 times in nine league games and are without Katseris, while their defence has been the meanest in the league. Karam's first priority is to tighten Le Havre up, so we lean below the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, mostly for Le Havre. Lorient sit back in a back three with wing-backs Kouassi and Sylla while the home side push for a first win, which fits the model's split.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, pulled down by referee Aurelien Petit's low average from only three games. A tense relegation game for a club in turmoil, under a new interim coach and with Seko suspended, looks more likely to be scrappy than calm.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. Lorient's attack is the weakest in the league, and Le Havre may be without midfielder Rassoul Ndiaye, so we lean a little below the model, especially on Lorient's side.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target. Lorient rarely test goalkeepers and lost Katseris, and Le Havre's attack has relied heavily on Josh Maja, so we lean a little lower.
